'''SX2 Media Labs LLC''' was a [[New York City]] based company which owned and published two United States technology magazines: ''[[Computer Shopper (US magazine)|Computer Shopper]]'' (1979–2009) and the once-yearly ''College Buying Guide''.

The company was formed in 2005 by David Sills, and Barry Schwimmer of Stoneybrook Capital, with the goal of becoming a "become a major information provider for technology enthusiasts".<ref>{{cite web
| url = http://www.sx2medialabs.com/
| title = SX2 Media Labs
| publisher = SX2 Media Labs LLC
| accessdate = 2008-03-11
}}</ref> Sills and Schwimmer previously worked together as Distance Education Company, which bought distance learning company Home Study Schools Corporation then was sold off in 2004.<ref>{{cite web
| url = http://www.sx2medialabs.com/team/
| title = SX2 Media Labs Management Team
| publisher = SX2 Media Labs LLC
| accessdate = 2008-03-11
}}</ref> On 2006-02-06, SX2 purchased ''Computer Shopper'' and ''College Buying Guide'' from [[CNET Networks]],<ref>{{cite web
| url = http://www.jegi.com/CNET-Sells-Computer-Shopper-Magazine-to-SX2-Media-Labs
| title = "CNET Networks Sells Computer Shopper Magazine to SX2 Media Labs" (press release)
| publisher = The Jordan, Edmiston Group, Inc.
| date = 2006-02-06
| accessdate = 2008-03-11
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110713101024/http://www.jegi.com/CNET-Sells-Computer-Shopper-Magazine-to-SX2-Media-Labs
| archive-date = 2011-07-13
| url-status = dead
}}</ref> and 20 days later, on 2006-02-26, Cyber Media (India) Ltd. obtained a 20% stake in SX2.<ref>{{cite web
| url = http://www.cybermedia.co.in/press/pressrelease18.html
| title = "CyberMedia Expands Globally - Acquires Strategic Stake in Computer Shopper" (press release)
| publisher = Cyber Media India Ltd.
| date = 2006-02-26
| accessdate = 2008-03-11
}}</ref> In 2009, SX2 Media Labs ceased publishing ''Computer Shopper'' magazine and went fully digital. In 2012, SX2 Media Labs sold the properties to Ziff Davis and ceased operations.

SX2 Media Labs LLC was a New York City based company which owned and published two United States technology magazines: Computer Shopper (1979–2009) and the once-yearly College Buying Guide.
The company was formed in 2005 by David Sills, and Barry Schwimmer of Stoneybrook Capital, with the goal of becoming a "become a major information provider for technology enthusiasts". Sills and Schwimmer previously worked together as Distance Education Company, which bought distance learning company Home Study Schools Corporation then was sold off in 2004. On 2006-02-06, SX2 purchased Computer Shopper and College Buying Guide from CNET Networks, and 20 days later, on 2006-02-26, Cyber Media (India) Ltd. obtained a 20% stake in SX2. In 2009, SX2 Media Labs ceased publishing Computer Shopper magazine and went fully digital. In 2012, SX2 Media Labs sold the properties to Ziff Davis and ceased operations.
